findings.claim: `{}` is not assignable to the generic type `E['Bindings']` without a cast, so this likely fails type-checking (or silently widens/erases the binding type).
findings.rationale: `E['Bindings']` is an unresolved generic indexed access; TypeScript only accepts an initializer that is assignable to every possible instantiation. If `Bindings` is e.g. `{ COUNTER: DurableObjectNamespace }`, the empty object literal does not satisfy it. If it does compile today it is only because of a looser constraint, and at runtime `c.env.COUNTER` is now `undefined` rather than a type error surface. Fairly confident this needs `= {} as E['Bindings']`.

findings.claim: A field initializer can be immediately overwritten by the constructor if it unconditionally does `this.env = options.env`, making the default ineffective when `options.env` is undefined.
findings.rationale: Class field initializers run before the constructor body. Unless the constructor guards with `options.env ?? {}` / `if (options.env)`, passing `{ env: undefined }` (or an options object without `env`) will set `this.env` back to `undefined` and defeat the purpose of this change. Worth verifying the Context constructor assignment; I can't see it in this hunk.

findings.claim: Behavior change: `c.env` is now a truthy empty object instead of `undefined` for callers that never supply bindings.
findings.rationale: Existing middleware/adapters that branch on `if (c.env)` or `c.env === undefined` (common in non-workers runtimes like Node/Deno where bindings are not provided) will now take the opposite branch. Also each Context construction allocates a fresh object per request, a small but per-request cost on a hot path. Moderate confidence this affects real callers.
